rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Aw” coordinates the two alternatives; it can express alternatives with both possible, or one excluded, and does not require doubt about whether one will occur.
rows.anchor: الدلالة على الترديد بين أحد الشيئين أو الأشياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan represented the tree as granting either angelhood or immortality, as he also says in 20:120.
rows.anchor: فمعنى الكلام أن الآكل من هذه الشجرة يكون ملكا وخالدا

words: مَا نَهَىٰكُمَا رَبُّكُمَا عَنْ هَٰذِهِ ٱلشَّجَرَةِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan insinuated that God's prohibition aimed at withholding one of those benefits; the implication is that God might intend to deprive them of both.
rows.anchor: ويستفاد من المقام أنه قد يريد حرمانهما من الأمرين جميعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adam did not yet know that immortality was impossible and that death, resurrection, and gathering were decreed for humanity; such knowledge comes through revelation.
rows.anchor: ولم يكن آدم قد علم حينئذ أن الخلود متعذر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After denying that God commands indecency in 7:28, the verse digresses to state the foundations of true religion; repeating “say” without a conjunction stresses this important contradiction of their claim.
rows.anchor: فصلت هذه الجملة عن التي قبلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qist means justice broadly: the balanced virtue in an act, free of excess and deficiency, and sound for welfare in both the near and long term.
rows.anchor: أي الفعل الذي هو وسط بين الإفراط والتفريط في الأشياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Examples of justice as a mean include monotheism between association and denial, just retaliation between impunity and collective vengeance, and beneficence between miserliness and extravagance.
rows.anchor: والقصاص من القاتل عدل بين إطلال الدماء

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses qist as the declaration “There is no god but God”; Ibn ʿĀshūr explains that this means monotheism is among the greatest forms of justice.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس أن القسط قول لا إلاه إلا هو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Clothing and food likewise require moderation: dress should cover nakedness and protect from heat or cold, while food should avoid both excessive restriction and gluttonous indulgence.
rows.anchor: والعدل هو اللباس الذي يستر العورة ويدفع أذى القر أو الحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This comprehensive command to justice refutes every claim that God commanded their indecent practices, since none of those acts is just.
rows.anchor: كلام جامع لإبطال كل ما يزعمون أن الله أمرهم به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command coordinates with “My Lord commands justice” and tells the audience explicitly to do the opposite of certain alleged divine commands; commanding the opposite also implicitly forbids them.
rows.anchor: أي قل لأولئك المخاطبين أقيموا وجوهكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Establish your faces” pictures complete attention to worship, like someone facing an important sight without turning right or left.
rows.anchor: وإقامة الوجوه تمثيل لكمال الإقبال على عبادة الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To establish the face means to make it firmly and actively oriented; “standing” can denote strength in action, as in saying that a market or prayer stood.
rows.anchor: وهو في إطلاق القيام على القوة في الفعل كما يقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God commands reverent worship at sacred places, not nakedness or other invented forms of honoring Him; associating idols with God in worship contradicts this command.
rows.anchor: ولم يأمر بتعظيمه ولا تعظيم مساجده بما سوى ذلك مثل التعري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith supports reverence in prayer: the worshipper converses with his Lord and should not spit in front of himself.
rows.anchor: المصلي يناجي ربه فلا يبصقن قبل وجهه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here “masjid” means any place set aside for worship; in Islamic usage it became the name of a specific, bounded place for prayer.
rows.anchor: عند كل مكان متخذ لعبادة الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since the audience then had no mosques apart from pilgrimage sanctuaries, the command concerns the Hajj rites and requires worshipping God alone there.
rows.anchor: ولم يكن لهم مساجد غير شعائر الحج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Polytheists placed Hubal on the Kaaba for the circumambulation, Isāf and Nāʾila at Ṣafā and Marwa for the saʿy, and some invoked Manāt at al-Mushallal; the command rejects these associations.
rows.anchor: ليكون الطواف بالكعبة لله ولهبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This command follows the denial that God commands indecency and the affirmation that He commands justice; it addresses polytheists, while believers must persist in it.
rows.anchor: عقب إنكار أن يأمر الله بالفحشاء من أحوالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Call upon Him” means worship Him, as in the verse about those whom people worship besides God.
rows.anchor: بمعنى العبادة أي اعبدوه كقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sincerity is purifying something from mixture; dīn here means obedience, from the expression “I obeyed so-and-so.” God is al-Dayyān, who subdues and makes all beings compliant.
rows.anchor: والإخلاص تمحيض الشيء من مخالطة غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Sincere to Him in religion” is a circumstantial phrase attached to the pronoun in “worship Him.”
rows.anchor: و { مخلصين } حال من الضمير في ادعوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parallel command in 98:5 confirms that the aim is to eliminate associating partners in worship, thereby realizing the justice named earlier in this verse.
rows.anchor: والمقصد منها إبطال الشرك في عبادة الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “As He began you, you will return” is an estimated circumstantial clause from the implied subject of “sincere”: worship with your return to God in view.
rows.anchor: مقدرين عودكم إليه وأن عودكم كبدئكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning focuses on returning to God to be judged for insincere worship and association; the comparison with the first creation recalls the resurrection they denied.
rows.anchor: وأدمج فيه قوله : { كما بدأكم } تذكيرا بإمكان البعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second creation is no more difficult than the first, as 50:15 and 30:27 argue against their supposed reason for rejecting resurrection.
rows.anchor: بأن ذلك الخلق ليس بأعجب من خلقهم الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone created them initially and will create them again, so He alone recompenses them and their idols can do nothing for them.
rows.anchor: فهو منفرد بالجزاء فلا يغني عنهم آلهتهم شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The kāf compares their return in creation to their beginning; mā is infinitival, yielding “you return with a new return like His beginning you.”
rows.anchor: تعودون عودا جديدا كبدئه إياكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison phrase precedes its verb, “you return,” to give the comparison prominence.
rows.anchor: على فعله ، وهو تعودون ، للاهتمام به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both occurrences of “a group” can be circumstantial from “you return”: people return to God as two groups, with the detailed division brought forward for warning and encouragement.
rows.anchor: فاكتفي عن إجمال الفريقين ثم تفصيلهما بالتفصيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Under the first parsing, one group was guided by God in worldly life and the other was doomed to error there, as the explanation about taking devils as allies shows.
rows.anchor: أن فريقا هداهم الله في الدنيا وفريقا حق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the groups are circumstantial from the implied subject of “sincere”: one group worships sincerely after guidance, while the other persists in idolatry.
rows.anchor: أي ادعوه مخلصين حال كونكم فريقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “He guided” describes the first group with its object pronoun omitted (“He guided them”); “doom was due” describes the second.
rows.anchor: أي هداكم الله ، وجملة : { حق عليهم الضلالة }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The division warns against error and following Satan, and urges people to seek guidance, which the verse attributes to God.
rows.anchor: وهذا كله إنذار من الوقوع في الضلالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The guided faction is like God's party, the successful; the erring faction is like Satan's party, the losers.
rows.anchor: وأن الفريق الخاسر هم الذين حقت عليه الضلالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both instances of “a group” precede their governing verbs to emphasize the detailed division.
rows.anchor: الأول والثاني على عامليهما للاهتمام بالتفصيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fāʾ marks the punishment as following immediately after the leaders' warning to their people.
rows.anchor: كان أخذ الرجفة إياهم عقب قولهم لقومهم ما قالوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr points back to the parallel account of Thamūd's punishment in 7:78.
rows.anchor: في نظيرها من قصة ثمود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people of Midian were struck by lightning from a cloud, the punishment called the “day of the shade” in 26:189.
rows.anchor: خرجت من ظلة ، وهي السحابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because Hūd's account calls it a cry, the sound is best understood as a splitting burst from a thing launched against another, not the impact sound of an earthquake.
rows.anchor: وقد عبر عن الرجفة في سورة هود بالصيحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prefers that both an earthquake and lightning struck them: the “quaking” was the earthquake and the “cry” the thunderbolt, consistent with the erased traces.
rows.anchor: والأظهر أن يكون أصابهم زلزال وصواعق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Those who denied Shuʿayb” begins a new independent sentence; its relative wording hints that their destruction and extinction were punishment for denial.
rows.anchor: مستأنفة ابتدائية ، والتعريف بالموصولية للإيماء إلى وجه بناء الخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghanā bi-l-makān means to reside there; hence maghnā names a people's dwelling place.
rows.anchor: ولذلك سمي مكان القوم مغنى

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says the Arabic poetry he surveyed uses ghanā for residence accompanied by comfortable living, perhaps from istighnā (being self-sufficient).
rows.anchor: ابن عطية : ( الذي استقريت من أشعار العرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison concerns the annihilation of their traces, not merely their death, which is true of every dead person; 10:24 gives a similar image.
rows.anchor: وهذا إنما يعنى به انمحاء آثارهم كما قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The total erasure suggests that earthquake and lightning burned their bodies, buried them, and overturned their dwellings beneath the earth.
rows.anchor: وهو يرجح أن يكون أصابهم زلزال مع الصواعق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fronting “those who denied Shuʿayb” strengthens the assertion if kāna is verbal; if it is a copula, the nominal sentence's stability supplies the emphasis.
rows.anchor: إذا اعتبرت { كانوا } فعلا ، واعتبر المسند فعليا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating “those who denied Shuʿayb” enumerates and awakens the Arab polytheist audience, indirectly warning them to avoid the fate of earlier idolaters and deniers, as stated explicitly in 47:10.
rows.anchor: والتكرير لقوله : { الذين كذبوا شعيبا } للتعديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The separating pronoun gives an additional restriction: the deniers, unlike Shuʿayb's followers, were the losers, exposing the chiefs' foolish claim that following him would mean loss.
rows.anchor: دون الذين اتبعوا شعيبا ، وذلك لإظهار سفه قول الملإ للعامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Commentators identify the Sabbath-town transgressors and the people who asked why the others preached as one group, citing the similarity to 2:65; Ibn ʿĀshūr says that conclusion is not certain.
rows.anchor: بأن الذين نسوا ما ذكروا به وعتوا عما نهوا عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The context allows one shared story, but similarity of wording and punishment also permits two groups to be considered as two stories for the lesson.
rows.anchor: كما أنه لا يمنع تشابه فريقين في العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun “upon them” refers to the previously discussed Jews, not the Sabbath-town inhabitants; the verse concerns the former and has no relation to the town's people.
rows.anchor: عائد إلى اليهود المتقدم ذكرهم بالضمير الراجع إليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taʾadhdhana derives from idhn, knowledge; the root relates to the ear as the organ of hearing, and its forms develop from that concrete noun.
rows.anchor: مشتق من الإذن وهو العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tafaʿʿala form usually marks reflexive or resultant action and can signal forceful occurrence; taʾadhdhana is also compared to tawwaʿada meaning awʿada.
rows.anchor: والمطاوعة مستعملة في معنى قوة حصول الفعل

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī leans toward the meaning “informed and announced”; on this reading the verb is suspended from its object by the oath lam in the response.
rows.anchor: وإلى هذا مال الطبري ، قال ابن عطية

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya finds the “informed” interpretation morphologically problematic because taʾadhdhana's relation to its subject and transitivity differ from aʿlama.
rows.anchor: إذ نسبة تأذن إلى الفاعل غير نسبة أعلم ، ويتبين ذلك من التعدي

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid glosses taʾadhdhana as swearing; al-Zamakhsharī explains this as God resolving, since someone resolved on an act speaks inwardly of it, hence the oath-like response.
rows.anchor: وعن مجاهد : { تأذن } تألى

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya considers the oath interpretation distant from the word itself, though the lam in the response led commentators to it.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية : ( وقادهم إلى هذا القول دخول اللام في الجواب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the phrase means “your Lord said,” announcing this through the tongues of His messengers.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس { تأذن ربك } قال ربك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse resumes the narrative of their circumstances; qattaʿnāhum can describe either blameworthy dispersal after unity or a praiseworthy division, depending on context, as in 7:160.
rows.anchor: فالتعويل على القرينة لا على لفظ التقطيع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The earth” here is generic and means across the regions of the earth.
rows.anchor: فالمراد من الأرض الجنس أي في أقطار الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Umam is the plural of umma in the sense of a community or group.
rows.anchor: و { أمما } جمع أمة بمعنى الجماعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the blameworthy reading, the verse refers to successive exiles: Assyrian capture of Israel and transfer to Babylon in 721 BCE, Babylonian capture of Judah and Jerusalem in 578 BCE, return in 530, then Roman expulsion under Titus in the early second century CE.
rows.anchor: ونقلهم إلى جبال انشور وأرض بابل سنة 721 قبل الميلاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saying some were righteous indicates that dispersal included both the guilty and others; God gave the righteous honor among the nations where they settled, as the following trials show.
rows.anchor: بأن التفريق شمل المذنبين وغيرهم ، وأن الله جعل للصالحين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Below that” includes everyone who fell short of righteousness, across varying degrees.
rows.anchor: وشمل قوله : { ومنهم دون ذلك } كل من لم يكن صالحا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The righteous kept Moses' law, affirmed later prophets, and believed Jesus; after Muhammad, only a few Jews such as ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām and Mukhayriq remained righteous by believing in him.
rows.anchor: و { الصالحون } هم المتمسكون بشريعة موسى والمصدقون للأنبياء المبعوثين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dūna dhālika can be an adverb describing an omitted “group” understood from minhum; alternatively, min may be a noun meaning “some,” with minhum as subject and dūna as predicate.
rows.anchor: على الظرفية وصفا لمحذوف دل عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reported possibility places the division during the Babylonian kingdoms: among those living in Babylon were righteous people such as Daniel and others, as well as a less righteous group.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن تكون الآية تشير إلى تفريقهم في الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording “some of them” suggests both groups were numerous.
rows.anchor: لأن التقسيم بمنهم مشعر بوفرة كلا الفريقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tests through good and bad revealed differing responses: patience and gratitude, or distress and disbelief; the terms mean things that please or trouble.
rows.anchor: أي أظهرنا مختلف حال بني إسرائيل في الصبر والشكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this reading, blessings and hardships detail the test and are acts of God distributed to the righteous and the rest.
rows.anchor: وعلى هذا يكون الحسنات والسيئات تفصيلا للبلوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Perhaps they will return” is an explanatory resumption: the hope is that they repent when recalling the periods of blessing and hardship or seeing the contrasting groups' fortunes.
rows.anchor: وجملة : { لعلهم يرجعون } استئناف بياني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Return here means repentance: turning back from breaking the covenant and disobedience.
rows.anchor: والرجوع هنا الرجوع عن نقض العهد وعن العصيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr offers his own alternative: the division may continue the account of divine favors, like 7:160, and mean that God multiplied them and settled them throughout the promised Holy Land.
rows.anchor: عودا إلى أخبار المنن عليهم ، فيكون كالبناء على قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this alternative, “the earth” means the promised land of Jerusalem; mentioning it here, unlike in 7:160, indicates that they inhabited all of it.
rows.anchor: أرض القدس الموعودة لهم أي لكثرناهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling some righteous is a fair acknowledgment after describing their groups' aggression and refusal to listen to admonition.
rows.anchor: إنصافا لهم بعد ذكر أحوال عدوان جماعاتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the favorable reading, God alternately treated them with mercy and requited the deeds of their masses.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى أن الله عاملهم مرة بالرحمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the preceding division means exile among enemy lands, “a successor came after them” follows that account and points to the Jews' return under Cyrus around 530 BCE.
rows.anchor: تفريع على قوله : { وقطعناهم } ( الأعراف : 168 ) إن كان المراد تقطيعهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Cyrus permitted Jews captured by Nebuchadnezzar to return; they rebuilt Jerusalem's temple through Nehemiah and Ezra and revived public reading of Moses' law.
rows.anchor: فإنه لما فتح بلاد أشور أذن لليهود الذين أسرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this reading, inheriting the book means renewing Torah practice through the scroll Ezra produced, Ezra being known in Muslim tradition as ʿUzayr.
rows.anchor: والمراد بإرث الكتاب إعادة مزاولتهم التوراة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taking worldly gain describes only some of the returned successor group, since its first members repented and included prophets and righteous people.
rows.anchor: ويكون أخذهم عرض الأدنى أخذ بعض الخلف لا جميعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the earlier division means multiplication and favor, the successors are descendants scattered after their ancestors' era, including the Jews in Medina at the rise of Islam; commentators incline to this reading.
rows.anchor: وإلى هذا المعنى في ( الخلف ) نحا المفسرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With a silent lām, khalaf means one who comes after another in place, work, or lineage, as context shows; it does not inherently denote an evil successor.
rows.anchor: والخلف بسكون اللام من يأتي بعد غيره

rows.speaker: النضر بن شميل
rows.claim: Al-Naḍr ibn Shumayl says silent-lām khalaf is not mostly used for an evil successor, contrary to many linguists.
rows.anchor: قاله النضر بن شميل ، خلافا لكثير من أهل اللغة

rows.speaker: كثير من أهل اللغة
rows.claim: Many linguists say silent-lām khalaf most often denotes a bad successor, while open-lām khalaf denotes a good one.
rows.anchor: إذ قالوا : الأكثر استعمال الخلف بسكون اللام

rows.speaker: البصريون
rows.claim: The Basran grammarians allow both pronunciations for a bad successor, but use only the open-lām form for a good successor.
rows.anchor: وقال البصريون : يجوز التحريك والإسكان في الرديء
